set.title: Connector plugin infrastructure
set.body:
Shared plugin infrastructure every external connector needs (Google Calendar, iCloud CalDAV, WhatsApp web bridge). Research: docs/research/google-calendar-integration.md, docs/research/apple-calendar-integration.md, docs/research/whatsapp-integration.md.

Four gaps in the current seam (src/nidaro/connectors/):

1. **Cursor persistence** — `Connector.sync(context, cursor)` has nowhere to store syncToken/ctag/sync-token high-water marks between runs.
2. **Encrypted credential storage** — Google OAuth refresh tokens, iCloud app-specific passwords: per-member secrets in PostgreSQL, never in source.
3. **Tombstone semantics** — deletions need a first-class marker on `ExternalRecord`/`SyncResult` (Google `status:"cancelled"`, CalDAV sync-report deletions).
4. **Connector-config intake** — per-household onboarding: enabled connectors, credential references, trigger word, polling cadence.

Children carry acceptance criteria. Calendar/WhatsApp integration tasks stay blocked until 1, 2 and 4 land.

set.title: WhatsApp group listening via web bridge
set.body:
Read-only WhatsApp group listening through a real Chrome session on a sacrificial number, per docs/research/whatsapp-integration.md §3.4 and the 2026-08-29 PoC (all four items resolved: binding bridge works, frames are E2E-encrypted so an in-page shim is required, gateway is wss://web.whatsapp.com/ws/chat, chrome-agent launch does NOT persist profiles).

Architecture: persistent Chromium (headed under Xvfb, normal-Chrome UA — headless gets gated) supervised outside nidaro; an observer asyncio task connects chrome-agent `CDPClient` to its CDP port; an in-page shim (`Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`) catches message arrival and ships events via `Runtime.addBinding`; events land in the same staging -> `WhatsAppConnector` -> `ExternalRecord` pipeline as the official webhook path (§5). Sends, trigger-word actions and LLM interpretation stay on the official Cloud API — the bridge is a dumb listener.

Human prerequisite: sacrificial number (child ticket). ToS posture: automated reading is unauthorized access under the consumer ToS — accepted by product decision 2026-08-29, risk-bounded by sacrificial number, read-only, low volume.

set.title: Cursor persistence for connector sync
set.body:
`Connector.sync(context, cursor)` is a pure function today; nothing stores the cursor between runs. Add a per-(household, connector) cursor row (`connector_cursors`: household_id, connector, cursor, updated_at) via repository -> service, and have `ConnectorService.sync` persist `next_cursor` after a successful run and hand it back on the next call.

Consumers: Google Calendar syncToken (with 410 GONE reset), iCloud CalDAV sync-token map, WhatsApp staging high-water id.

Acceptance: cursor survives a service restart; reset path (invalid token) testable.

set.title: Encrypted credential storage for connector secrets
set.body:
Secrets at rest: Google OAuth refresh tokens, iCloud app-specific passwords, per-connector tokens. Symmetric encryption keyed from Settings/env, ciphertext in PostgreSQL, plaintext never logged or migrated. No secrets in source control (AGENTS.md).

Acceptance: repository round-trips a secret; key-rotation path documented; no plaintext in logs/migrations.

set.title: Tombstone semantics on ExternalRecord
set.body:
`ExternalRecord` carries no deletion signal, so domain application can upsert but never delete. Add a tombstone marker (flag on ExternalRecord or a record-type convention) so calendar domain application removes mirrors. Sources: Google `status:"cancelled"` events, CalDAV sync-collection REPORT deletions.

Acceptance: deleting an external event removes the mirror in nidaro via the application service; tested.

set.title: Per-household connector config intake
set.body:
Per-household connector onboarding: which connectors are enabled, credential references (ids, not inline secrets), WhatsApp trigger word, polling cadence. Config lives in PostgreSQL behind the service boundary, not env-only Settings.

Acceptance: enabling a connector for a household is one service call; the scheduler honors per-household cadence.

set.title: Persistent-Chromium supervisor with CDP attach
set.body:
Run Chromium with a persistent --user-data-dir (systemd unit or compose service with a volume) exposing CDP on a local port; headed (Xvfb on servers) with a normal-Chrome UA — WhatsApp gates on the HeadlessChrome UA. A small supervisor connects chrome-agent `CDPClient(ws_url=get_ws_url(port))` to it and detects browser death for reconnect.

PoC gotcha (docs/research/whatsapp-integration.md §3.4): chrome-agent's launch/registry wipes instance session dirs on stop, logging the device out. QR pairing must survive restarts — hence our own profile dir, not the registry.

Acceptance: supervisor restart keeps the linked session; observer reconnects automatically after a browser crash.

set.title: WhatsAppConnector: staging drain to ExternalRecords
set.body:
Drain the WhatsApp staging table into `ExternalRecord`s via `WhatsAppConnector` (name "whatsapp", external_id = message id, payload per docs/research/whatsapp-integration.md §5.3, bridge events tagged source:"web_bridge"), registered in the `ConnectorRegistry`; cursor = staging high-water id. Domain writes (commitments/tasks) go through application services only; deterministic trigger parsing stays on the official-DM path (§5.4).

Acceptance: connector sync round-trips staged group messages into ExternalRecords idempotently; the connector writes no domain tables.

set.title: Procure sacrificial WhatsApp number for the bridge
set.body:
Acquire and register a prepaid SIM / sacrificial WhatsApp number for the web bridge. Never a family member's personal number — the accepted ToS blast radius is this number only.

Steps: register the number in WhatsApp; add it to the family group(s) nidaro should listen to; complete one device link against the PoC browser; while in Settings -> Linked devices, unlink any stale PoC sessions.

set.title: In-page WhatsApp shim + observer task
set.body:
Minimal in-page shim injected via `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`: watch message arrival (DOM MutationObserver first; module-store hook as a later upgrade for structured data — wamid, sender, type) and ship JSON events via `Runtime.addBinding` -> `Runtime.bindingCalled` into an asyncio observer task. PoC-proven pipe, ~1s latency end to end. Observer writes raw events to the WhatsApp staging table.

Acceptance: a message in any chat of the linked number reaches staging within ~2s; shim survives page reloads; observer reconnects after a browser restart.

set.title: Google Calendar connector (OAuth + syncToken sync)
set.body:
Implement GoogleCalendarConnector per docs/research/google-calendar-integration.md:

- OAuth per family member (web flow; NO service accounts for personal Gmail), refresh tokens encrypted at rest (NIDAR-cy2xmf).
- syncToken incremental sync as the connector cursor, 410 GONE full re-sync fallback (NIDAR-gdcw4e).
- Direct httpx against the Calendar v3 JSON API (skip google-api-python-client / httplib2); google-auth only for token handling if needed.
- Polling via the Taskiq scheduler — watch channels need a public HTTPS endpoint, skipped by design.
- ExternalRecords applied through CalendarService; tombstones handle status:"cancelled" (NIDAR-ryzjms).
- Writes (assistant create/update tool) through a service-boundary Google write service: etag If-Match concurrency, extendedProperties.private mirror-loop markers, sendUpdates on attendee events.

Open decision before launch (record in ticket comments when made): publish the Google app production-unverified (warning screen + 100-user cap, stable tokens) vs Testing mode (refresh tokens expire every 7 days) — the deployment blocker called out in the research doc.

set.title: Apple iCloud Calendar connector (CalDAV polling)
set.body:
Implement IcloudCalendarConnector per docs/research/apple-calendar-integration.md:

- Poll iCloud CalDAV (caldav.icloud.com) with per-member app-specific passwords (Basic auth over TLS; 2FA required on the Apple ID), encrypted at rest (NIDAR-cy2xmf).
- sync-collection REPORT with the sync-token map as connector cursor (NIDAR-gdcw4e); getctag fallback; RFC 6578 token invalidation happens on iCloud — full re-sync path must work.
- Scheduler-driven cadence (~15 min floor); no push exists, polling only.
- Parse ICS with icalendar; watch the /freeassociation.sourceforge.net/ TZID vendor-prefix trap; stable external_id = UID (+recurrence-id); content_hash for change detection.
- Read-only v1; CalDAV write-back deferred (etag conflicts, flaky recurring-event history in library tests — verify against a live account first if attempted).

Acceptance: new/changed/deleted iCloud events mirror into the calendar domain through CalendarService within one poll cycle.

set.title: [cal] Base family calendar v1
set.body:
## Destination

The base family calendar is live at `/calendar`: month, week, and day views over the household's activities, with minimal recurring activities, seed/demo data, and an add-activity form. It's a working initial step — structured so edit/delete, richer recurrence, and external sync can extend it later.

## Notes

- **Execution rides the map.** The destination is an implemented page, so this map's later tickets are build tasks, not only decisions. (Override of plan-only default, agreed at charting.)
- Domain: family assistant. Boundary is route/tool/worker → service → repository → database; PostgreSQL holds family state.
- UI law is [DESIGN.md](../../DESIGN.md): server-rendered Jinja2 + HTMX partials, no build step, tokens only (`--cat-calendar`, `.dot`, `.card`). Skills per ticket: grilling + domain-modeling for decisions, prototype for `[cal-3]`.
- Existing ground: `Event` model (`events` table: title, description, tz-aware starts_at/ends_at, location, status, participants M2M), `CalendarService`/repository with only `upcoming(7d)` + `create`, assistant tools for both, **no** calendar HTTP routes, `/calendar` nav slot renders a placeholder. Single household via `services.household.get_household()`.
- Future merge point: Google/Apple connector sync (own epic) will pour external events into the same `events` table — see `docs/research/google-calendar-integration.md` and `docs/research/apple-calendar-integration.md`. Recurrence expansion decided in `[cal-2]` should align with their read-time approach.
- Charting decisions (this session): destination = implemented page; v1 shows everything in `events` (no kind/activity filter — "not meetings" stays a usage convention); recurring activities are in v1 (weekly repeats, read-time expansion, no per-occurrence exceptions); page = read views + add-activity form + seed/demo data; handle prefix `cal`.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: [title](link): gist -->

## Not yet specified

- **Build slices for the destination** — data-model migration; range query + API + seeds; month/week/day page with HTMX navigation; add-activity form. Graduate into task tickets as `[cal-1]`–`[cal-4]` close.
- **Per-occurrence exceptions and edit/delete** — moving or cancelling one instance of a series; editing activities. Hangs on `[cal-2]`'s storage choice.
- **Externally synced events on this calendar** — how Google/Apple events merge in, and whether a family-relevance filter is needed once personal calendars pour in. Hangs on the connector epic; the "activity vs meeting" question lives here.
- **Category/color system for activities** — person-colored vs category tokens. Hangs on `[cal-3]`'s prototype reaction and later domains (school, meals) feeding the calendar.

## Out of scope

- **External calendar sync implementation** (Google/Apple) — has its own epic ("Connector plugin infrastructure") and research docs.
- **Reminders/notifications** — no nags in v1.
- **User accounts/auth** — single seeded household, as today.
- **Fancy calendar interactions** — drag-to-reschedule, mini-months, multi-calendar overlays.

set.title: [cal-1] What is a v1 activity?
set.body:
## Question

What is a v1 activity? The `Event` model already has title, description, `starts_at`/`ends_at` (tz-aware), location, status, and participants (M2M to family members). Decide what v1 adds or drops:

- Which fields must exist for the v1 content (recurring activities like volleyball practice and dancing lessons, plus one-off special days)?
- Is there an all-day flag ("no school today"), and how is it modeled (bool vs date-only semantics)?
- How does a person express recurrence in the add-activity form ("every week on Mon & Thu at 16:00") — what does that look like as input?
- Which existing fields stay unused in v1 (description? status?) rather than getting UI?
- What migration does the `events` table need?

Out of scope for this ticket: expansion mechanics (`[cal-2]`), page visuals (`[cal-3]`), API/seeds/timezone (`[cal-4]`).

set.title: [cal-2] How do recurring activities land on the calendar?
set.body:
## Question

How do recurring activities land on the calendar? `[cal-1]` decides what recurrence a user can enter; this decides how the system stores, expands, and serves it:

- Storage shape: weekday-set + time (e.g. `by_weekday=[mon,thu], time=16:00`) vs a generic RRULE string. Pick the smallest thing that covers "every week on these days at this time" and stays honest for later extension.
- Read-time expansion: expanded at query time over a bounded window (which window? e.g. the queried range, clamped). Never persist infinite expansions — the Apple/Google sync research (`docs/research/apple-calendar-integration.md`, `google-calendar-integration.md`) already prescribes deterministic read-time expansion for external events; align so both sources share one mechanism.
- What expanded instances look like to callers of the range query (synthetic ids? instance rows vs computed?).
- State explicitly what v1 excludes: per-occurrence exceptions (moved/cancelled single instances), calendar-level exceptions, DST/timezone edges beyond the obvious.

Boundary reminder: expansion is deterministic domain/service logic, not LLM work.

set.title: [cal-3] What does the base calendar page look like?
set.body:
## Question

What does the base calendar page at `/calendar` look like? Build a cheap, rough, concrete prototype (HTML/HTMX with static demo data is fine) to react to:

- Month grid (default: current month), week view, day view — and the switching model: view tabs, prev/next navigation, "today" button, deep-linkable state (query param? path?).
- How an activity renders in each view: a month cell (dot + short title? time?), a week column, a day list. How recurring instances appear ("Volleyball · Thu 16:00" repeated).
- Whether participants show (name? `.avatar-stack`?) and where.
- Empty days and empty months; today's highlighting; month/week boundaries that spill across months.
- Everything on DESIGN.md tokens only (`--cat-calendar`, `.dot`, `.card`, `.btn`), server-rendered + HTMX partials, no build step.

React to the prototype, then write down the decided layout. This ticket decides appearance and interaction, not backend mechanics (`[cal-2]`, `[cal-4]`).

set.title: [cal-4] What is the v1 backend surface?
set.body:
## Question

What is the v1 backend surface for the calendar? The decisions above fix what an activity is and how recurrence expands; this fixes how code serves it:

- Repository/service: a date-range query (household, from, to → events + expanded instances), replacing or complementing `upcoming(7d)`.
- HTTP API: `GET /api/v1/calendar/events?from=&to=` (+ POST create?) — or UI-only server routes feeding HTMX partials, with the API trailing until a consumer needs it. Decide which exists in v1.
- Where the add-activity form posts: HTMX partial swap vs JSON API call.
- Household timezone: which timezone renders days/weeks, where it is configured (household setting vs server default), and what the default is. Events are stored tz-aware UTC.
- The seed/demo data set: a realistic family week (volleyball practice, dancing lessons, one-off specials) for dev and demos; where the seeder lives.

Keep the boundary: route → service → repository → database. No SQL in routes.

set.title: [mealplan] Meal planner: week view and dish configuration
set.body:
## Destination

A merged vertical slice in nidaro: a `meals` domain backed by PostgreSQL, a rolling 7-day **week view** page for planning, and a **dish configuration** page for typical meals. Manual planning only — no AI anywhere in this slice, but the data model leaves room for a later AI planning map.

## Notes

- **This map carries execution.** Destination is working code, so `wayfinder:task` children build the slice; decision children still resolve before their dependent build tickets.
- Domain conventions: `route/tool/worker -> service -> repository -> database`; all I/O async; no microservices; PostgreSQL authoritative. See `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`.
- UI is server-rendered Jinja2 + HTMX, tokens from `DESIGN.md` / `tokens.css`; no hex/font literals outside tokens.
- Quality: `aufsicht fast` during work, `aufsicht full` before complete; ruff via `.quality/toolchain.lock` pins.
- Ubiquitous language lives in `CONTEXT.md` (Dish, Planned meal, Slot). Consult **grilling** + **domain-modeling** for grilling tickets, **prototype** for prototype tickets, **tdd** for build tickets.
- Decisions settled while charting (do not re-litigate):
  - Meal planning is **its own domain**; planned meals never become calendar Events (would overload the calendar).
  - Week view: rolling window of **7 days from today**, prev/next arrows shift by one week, "back to today" reset.
  - Slots per day: **breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks**.
  - A slot may hold **multiple planned meals**; entries stack with a remove action (feel to be validated by the week-view prototype).
  - Planning interaction: per-slot inline form — pick an existing Dish from a dropdown, **or** type a one-off name (no Dish required).
  - Dish fields: **name, notes, tags** (tags give the later AI map structure). Full CRUD on the config page; delete confirms via HTMX.
  - Copy-on-plan: a planned meal snapshots the dish name; deleting a Dish never dangles history.
  - AI planning and its interaction model are a **separate later map** — this map only shapes the seams (structured fields), builds nothing AI-shaped.

## Decisions so far

_(none yet — map just charted)_

## Not yet specified

- A meals tile on the home dashboard ("what's for dinner tonight") — only specifiable once the week view exists and shows real shape.

## Out of scope

- **AI-generated plans, tech proposals, assistant tools for meals** — postponed by the user to a dedicated later map; this map only leaves structured seams.
- **Shopping list derivation** from the plan — beyond this destination; its own effort if wanted.
- **Recipe/ingredient detail** (steps, quantities) — Dish stays name + notes + tags for now.
- **Calendar/Event coupling** — ruled out explicitly; meals never render as events.
- **Auth / multi-household** — repo-wide concern, not this map's.

set.title: [mealplan-1] Prototype: week view layout
set.body:
## Question

How should the rolling 7-day **week view** look and behave with stacked entries? The settled rules: today-first window, four slots (breakfast/lunch/dinner/snacks), multiple planned meals per slot shown as a small stack, per-slot inline form (dish dropdown *or* one-off name), remove per entry, prev/next shift the window by a week with a back-to-today reset.

Produce a cheap, rough, clickable HTML/HTMX stub (static or throwaway route) to react to. Judge: density of 7 columns on desktop *and* mobile, how stacked entries read, where the add-form lives without clutter, how one-off names differ visually from dish-backed entries.

Call the Skill tool with "prototype". Link the stub as an asset on resolution.

set.title: [mealplan-2] Prototype: dish configuration page
set.body:
## Question

How should the **dish configuration** page look and behave? Settled scope: list of dishes (name, notes, tags), create + edit + delete (delete confirms via HTMX), tags as a simple input.

Produce a cheap, rough, clickable stub to react to. Judge: list-vs-card layout for a family-sized set of dishes (tens, not thousands), how notes and tags render without noise, edit-in-place vs edit-on-separate-view.

Call the Skill tool with "prototype". Link the stub as an asset on resolution.

set.title: [mealplan-3] Build: meals domain (models, migration, repository, service)
set.body:
## Work

Build the `meals` domain following the house pattern (`service -> repository -> PostgreSQL`, async all the way):

- `Dish`: name, notes, tags; household-scoped like every domain.
- `PlannedMeal`: date, slot (breakfast/lunch/dinner/snacks), nullable dish reference, snapshotted name (copy-on-plan — deleting a Dish never dangles history). Multiple planned meals per date+slot are allowed; no uniqueness constraint.
- Alembic migration, repository, application service, and tests first (consult the **tdd** skill).

Schema shape is settled in the map Notes — build it, don't redesign it. AI stays out; tags and structured fields are the only seams.

set.title: [mealplan-4] Build: week view page
set.body:
## Work

Build the **week view** page from the layout the prototype settled: rolling 7-day window from today, four slots per day, stacked planned meals, per-slot inline add form (dish dropdown or one-off name), remove per entry, prev/next window shift by one week via URL offset, back-to-today reset.

Jinja2 + HTMX only, tokens from `DESIGN.md`; UI route calls the meals application service, never repositories. Tests follow the **tdd** skill.

set.title: [mealplan-5] Build: dish configuration page
set.body:
## Work

Build the **dish configuration** page from the prototype's settled layout: full CRUD over dishes (name, notes, tags), HTMX confirm on delete. Same rules as the week-view ticket: Jinja2 + HTMX, design tokens, service boundary, tests via the **tdd** skill.

set.title: [mealplan-6] Finish: nav, seed data, smoke test, quality gates
set.body:
## Work

Make the slice feel finished: wire the meals pages into the shell nav (replacing whatever placeholder path they used), extend `nidaro-seed` with a handful of typical dishes and a partly-planned current week so the UI shows real content, extend `scripts/e2e_ui_shell.sh` with a meals smoke pass, and run `aufsicht full` clean.

When this closes, the map's destination is reached.

text:
## Resolution

A v1 activity is an Event on the family calendar. Everything in `events` shows up — no kind filter; "activity" is the user-facing word for Event. Decided shape:

- **Fields with a form/UI**: title (required); when — either a single date with start–end time, or a weekly pattern (chosen weekdays + fixed start–end time); all-day toggle; participants (optional multi-select of family members); location (optional free text).
- **All-day**: `is_all_day` bool on `events`, default false; when set, the form hides time inputs.
- **Recurrence input in v1**: "every week on chosen weekdays, fixed start–end time" only. No series end date, no fortnightly/monthly cadences. An all-day activity can recur weekly too (pattern without times).
- **Participants semantics**: empty participants = whole household; renders without a person label.
- **Without v1 UI**: `description` and `status` — columns stay, status remains `scheduled`, no form fields.
- **Migration**: `0002_*`, additive only — `is_all_day` now; recurrence columns as shaped by [cal-2].

Consequences on the map: [cal-2] stores/expands exactly the weekly-weekdays + optional-time-window pattern; [cal-3] must render all-day entries and household-wide (participant-less) activities.

text:
## Resolution

Three variants prototyped on the throwaway /prototype/week-view route (in-memory stub store, HTMX, floating switcher, keyboard arrows). Verdict after live reaction: **one responsive page — A (week grid) on wide screens, B (day cards) on narrow**. The two share the window nav and the per-slot interaction model: pick an existing dish from a dropdown, or type a one-off name; entries stack per slot with a remove action. set.body:
## Symptom

Calling `ensure_household` outside an active session context returns a detached `Household`; `HouseholdView.model_validate` then lazy-loads `members` and raises `DetachedInstanceError` (sqlalchemy e20). Reproduced while live-verifying the meals domain ([mealplan-3] resolution comment).

## Suspected cause

The repository returns the ORM object after its session closes, and `Household.members` is a lazy relationship that `HouseholdView` tries to read. Calendar/tasks views avoid this by not serializing relationships.

## Notes

Not blocking the meals slice. Likely fix shape: eager-load (selectinload) or drop `members` from the view — triager's call.

## Destination

A merged vertical slice in nidaro: a `meals` domain backed by PostgreSQL, a rolling 7-day **week view** page for planning, and a **dish configuration** page for typical meals. Manual planning only — no AI anywhere in this slice, but the data model leaves room for a later AI planning map.

## Notes

- **This map carries execution.** Destination is working code, so `wayfinder:task` children build the slice; decision children still resolve before their dependent build tickets.
- Domain conventions: `route/tool/worker -> service -> repository -> database`; all I/O async; no microservices; PostgreSQL authoritative. See `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`.
- UI is server-rendered Jinja2 + HTMX, tokens from `DESIGN.md` / `tokens.css`; no hex/font literals outside tokens.
- Quality: `aufsicht fast` during work, `aufsicht full` before complete; ruff via `.quality/toolchain.lock` pins.
- **Commit regularly** (standing preference from the human): land small commits per slice instead of one big drop at the end.
- Ubiquitous language lives in `CONTEXT.md` (Dish, Planned meal, Slot). Consult **grilling** + **domain-modeling** for grilling tickets, **prototype** for prototype tickets, **tdd** for build tickets.
- Decisions settled while charting (do not re-litigate):
  - Meal planning is **its own domain**; planned meals never become calendar Events (would overload the calendar).
  - Week view: rolling window of **7 days from today**, prev/next arrows shift by one week, "back to today" reset.
  - Slots per day: **breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks**.
  - A slot may hold **multiple planned meals**; entries stack with a remove action (feel to be validated by the week-view prototype).
  - Planning interaction: per-slot inline form — pick an existing Dish from a dropdown, **or** type a one-off name (no Dish required).
  - Dish fields: **name, notes, tags** (tags give the later AI map structure). Full CRUD on the config page; delete confirms via HTMX.
  - Copy-on-plan: a planned meal snapshots the dish name; deleting a Dish never dangles history.
  - AI planning and its interaction model are a **separate later map** — this map only shapes the seams (structured fields), builds nothing AI-shaped.

## Decisions so far

- [Build: week view page](NIDAR-gy8gtf): merged 4e8298a — one responsive page at /meals (grid → day cards below 66rem), `?w=` window offset, HTMX add/remove; Annotated-Depends (suppressions gate rejects new noqa B008).
- [Build: dish configuration page](NIDAR-cqsxc0): merged 078da9e — table + expanding-row labeled editor at /meals/dishes; deptry `known_first_party` config fix in pyproject.toml unblocked the ratchet for new first-party modules.
- [Finish: nav, seed data, smoke test, quality gates](NIDAR-h4trzx): merged a5ee6d0 — prototypes deleted (captures kept on prototype/* branches), seeder seeds dishes + partly-planned week, e2e meals pass; merged main green on all 14 gates. **Destination reached.**

- [Build: meals domain (models, migration, repository, service)](NIDAR-2vy9hm): dishes + planned meals merged; copy-on-plan via name snapshot + ON DELETE SET NULL; protocol-typed service seam; aufsicht fast+full green.
- [Prototype: week view layout](NIDAR-2kr73c): one responsive page — **week grid on wide screens, day cards on narrow**; per-slot dish-dropdown or one-off form; palette interaction rejected. Primary source on branch `prototype/week-view`.
- [Prototype: dish configuration page](NIDAR-269qmn): **table rows + C-style labeled editor unfolding as an expanding row** — name / tag pills / notes columns, one add-form on top, HTMX confirm on delete; cards and the master-detail list rejected (its editor form adopted). Primary source on branch `prototype/dishes`.


## Out of scope

- **Meals tile on the home dashboard** ("what's for dinner tonight") — surfaced as fog while charting; sits past this destination (week view + dish config). Its own effort if wanted.

- **AI-generated plans, tech proposals, assistant tools for meals** — postponed by the user to a dedicated later map; this map only leaves structured seams.
- **Shopping list derivation** from the plan — beyond this destination; its own effort if wanted.
- **Recipe/ingredient detail** (steps, quantities) — Dish stays name + notes + tags for now.
- **Calendar/Event coupling** — ruled out explicitly; meals never render as events.
- **Auth / multi-household** — repo-wide concern, not this map's.
